findings.source_quote: νόμος Θεοῦ ἐστὶν ὁ δοθεὶς εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον· ὁ δὲ νόμος οὗτος υἱὸς Θεοῦ ἐστὶ κηρυχθεὶς εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς
findings.english_quote: Hermas here identifies the “law of God” with the Son of God and his proclamation. The term “law” in this Similitude functions as God’s binding instruction embodied and announced by the Son, not as a narrow reference to the Mosaic code.
findings.issue: Footnote a goes beyond the identification preserved in the main text. The source identifies the law with the Son, who is proclaimed; it does not additionally identify the law with his proclamation or say that the Son announces the instruction. The note turns the Son from the subject of a passive proclamation into its agent without disclosing that interpretive expansion.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the unsupported explanation with a source-limited note, for example: “Hermas identifies this law with the Son of God, who is proclaimed to the ends of the earth. The translation retains that identification rather than replacing it with ‘the message about the Son.’” Any broader account of the law’s relationship to Mosaic instruction should be explicitly identified as contextual interpretation and supported separately. Review the related theological rationale for the same conflation.

findings.english_quote: The compound intensifies struggle; “grappled” conveys close, strenuous combat.
findings.issue: The lexical rationale attributes intensification to the compound itself without supporting contextual evidence. The compound expresses wrestling or grappling with an opponent; its morphology alone does not establish an intensified degree of struggle. The main-text rendering “grappled” does not require this claim.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain “grappled” as a candidate, but revise the rationale to describe the observable wrestling imagery: “The verb describes wrestling or grappling with the devil; ‘grappled’ preserves that combat imagery.” Do not infer intensification solely from the compound form.

findings.source_quote: νόμος Θεοῦ ἐστὶν ὁ δοθεὶς εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον· ὁ δὲ νόμος οὗτος υἱὸς Θεοῦ ἐστὶ κηρυχθεὶς εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς
findings.english_quote: Hermas here identifies the “law of God” with the Son of God and his proclamation. The term “law” in this Similitude functions as God’s binding instruction embodied and announced by the Son, not as a narrow reference to the Mosaic code.
findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this note adds an identification with the proclamation and makes the Son the agent announcing the instruction. The selected clause instead identifies the law with the Son and describes the Son as proclaimed. The simplified main text preserves that distinction, but its note does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a source-limited explanation, such as: “Hermas identifies this law with the Son of God, who is proclaimed to the ends of the earth. The translation keeps this identification rather than saying only ‘the message about the Son.’” Qualify and separately support any broader interpretation concerning Mosaic instruction. Review the related theological rationale as well.

findings.english_quote: The compound intensifies struggle; “grappled” conveys close, strenuous combat.
findings.issue: The supplied lexical metadata infers intensification from compound morphology without evidence. It also explains “grappled,” whereas this edition actually prints “struggled against,” leaving the simplified choice without its own source-based explanation of the wrestling imagery.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the morphological intensification claim and document the actual simplified wording. Compare “struggled against” with a source-transparent candidate such as “wrestled with the devil,” explaining how the selected wording preserves the combat imagery. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: οἱ δὲ χλωρὰς ἐπιδεδωκότες οἵας ἔλαβον
findings.english_quote: Those who returned their rods as green as when they received them
findings.issue: The source compares the returned green rods with the rods as received, not merely their degree of greenness. “As green as” narrows the comparison to color or vitality and loses the broader unchanged-condition statement, which matters after the preceding distinctions involving shoots and fruit.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “Those who returned their green rods just as they received them.” This preserves both their greenness and the comparison with their received condition; review the proposed wording before adoption.

summary: Both editions require limited revisions. The standard main text covers the selected clauses; the simplified text narrows the final comparison concerning the rods. Both preserve Michael’s identity, speaker attribution, the difficult law–Son identification, the suffering contrast and its negations, and contextual repentance without adding confession or a uniform Godward condition. The bracketed sentence and its unexplained status in the supplied normalized source are honestly disclosed; no witness-omission claim is made. These findings concern the supplied working source and editorial disclosures, not authentication of unseen editions or manuscripts. Proposed corrections remain subject to fresh review.
